question.text: A light charged particle is revolving in a circle of radius $r$ in electrostatic attraction of a static heavy particle with opposite charge How does the magnetic field vary at the centre of the circle due to the moving charge depend on $r ?$

solution.text: $$ \begin{aligned} &\begin{array}{l} F_{\text {centripetal }}=m r \omega^{2}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0}} \cdot \frac{q_{1} q_{2}}{r^{2}} \\ \therefore \quad \omega^{2}=\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0} m} \cdot \frac{q_{1} q_{2}}{r^{3}} \Rightarrow \omega=\sqrt{\frac{q_{1} q_{2}}{4 \pi \varepsilon_{0} m r^{3}}} \end{array}\\ &\omega \propto \frac{1}{r^{3 / 2}} \end{aligned} $$ Current produced due to moving $q_{1}$ $$ i=\frac{\omega}{2 \pi} q_{1} $$ Thus, magnetic field due to motion of $q_{1}$ in circular path at point $\underline{O}$ $B=\frac{\mu_{0}}{2} \cdot \frac{i}{r}=\frac{\mu_{0}}{2} \cdot \frac{\omega q_{1}}{2 \pi r} \quad[$ using $\mathrm{Eq} \cdot(\mathrm{ii})]$ Hence, $B \propto \frac{\omega}{r}$ Magnetic field $B \propto \frac{1}{r^{3 / 2}}$ $[$ using Eq. (i) ]
